section_summary: This section documents official diplomatic correspondence and political reports regarding the Japanese Imperial Family between 1930 and 1934. Key matters include the marriage and international goodwill tour of Prince and Princess Takamatsu, the birth of Princess Atsuko in 1931, and diplomatic incidents relating to imperial prestige such as a defamatory article in Canton. The concluding documents focus on the historic birth of Crown Prince Akihito in December 1933, marked by U.S. congratulatory broadcasts and detailed diplomatic assessments of its stabilizing effect on Japanese internal politics.

subfiles.about: Reporting the itinerary and plans for Prince and Princess Takamatsu's extended journey to Europe and the United States following their wedding.
subfiles.from: William R. Castle, Jr. (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Castle reports Prince Takamatsu will tour Europe and North America after his wedding, to return the Duke of Gloucester's visit and present the Chrysanthemum Order to Spain's King.
subfiles.title: Proposed Visit of Prince and Princess Takamatsu to Europe and the United States

subfiles.about: Requesting embassy authorization for a monetary contribution toward a Diplomatic Corps wedding gift for Prince Takamatsu.
subfiles.from: William R. Castle, Jr. (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Castle reports Prince Takamatsu's February 4, 1930 wedding and a proposed Diplomatic Corps gift, and requests a special allowance for the Embassy's share of about $25.
subfiles.title: Diplomatic Corps Wedding Gift for Prince Takamatsu

subfiles.about: Authorizing a special allowance of $25.00 for the embassy's contribution toward Prince Takamatsu's wedding gift.
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr (For the Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Department grants the Tokyo Embassy a $25.00 allowance toward the Diplomatic Corps wedding gift for Prince Takamatsu.
subfiles.title: Grant of Allowance for Diplomatic Corps Wedding Present
subfiles.to: William R. Castle, Jr. (American Ambassador, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Reporting the exact contribution required for Prince Takamatsu's wedding gift and requesting authorization of $16.92.
subfiles.from: William R. Castle, Jr. (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Castle reports that the final per-mission contribution for the Diplomatic Corps wedding gift to Prince Takamatsu amounted to exactly 34 yen. He requests Department authorization for $16.92, which represents the equivalent in U.S. currency at current exchange rates.
subfiles.title: Cost of Diplomatic Corps Gift for Prince Takamatsu

subfiles.about: Transmitting an autograph letter from Emperor Hirohito announcing the marriage of Prince Takamatsu to Lady Kikuko Tokugawa.
subfiles.from: Katsuji Debuchi (Japanese Ambassador, Washington)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Debuchi transmits an autograph letter from Emperor Hirohito, alongside an English translation, for presentation to President Hoover. The letter officially announces that the marriage of Prince Nobuhito Takamatsu to Lady Kikuko Tokugawa was solemnized at the Imperial Palace in Tokyo on February 4, 1930. Japanese text and departmental routing sheets accompany the note.
subfiles.title: Emperor Hirohito's Announcement of the Marriage of Prince Takamatsu
subfiles.to: Joseph P. Cotton (Acting Secretary of State, Washington)

subfiles.about: Transmitting President Hoover's autograph letter of congratulations in response to Emperor Hirohito's marriage announcement.
subfiles.from: Francis White (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Department forwards President Hoover's April 9, 1930 autograph reply for Castle to present to the Emperor, congratulating him on Prince Takamatsu's marriage.
subfiles.title: Presidential Reply to the Emperor on the Marriage of Prince Takamatsu
subfiles.to: William R. Castle, Jr. (American Ambassador, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Informing the Japanese Ambassador that President Hoover's congratulatory letter has been forwarded to Tokyo for presentation.
subfiles.from: Francis White (For the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Francis White acknowledges Ambassador Debuchi's April 4, 1930 note; Hoover's reply to the Emperor's announcement was sent to Tokyo for delivery.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of the Emperor's Autograph Letter

subfiles.about: Reporting on the visit of Prince Chichibu to Japanese communities along the South Manchuria Railway.
subfiles.from: Myrl S. Myers (American Consul General, Mukden)
subfiles.summary: Consul General Myers reports Prince Chichibu's May 1930 tour of South Manchuria Railway communities, where Chang Hsueh-liang met him at a Japanese reception; he stayed within the railway zone.
subfiles.title: Visit of Prince Chichibu to Manchuria

subfiles.about: Transmitting notes exchanged with the Japanese Foreign Office regarding the delivery of President Hoover's letter to the Emperor.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Chargé Neville forwards notes exchanged with Shidehara confirming arrangements to present President Hoover's letter on Prince Takamatsu's marriage to the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Presentation of Presidential Letter to the Emperor of Japan

subfiles.about: Reporting on the state visit of Prince and Princess Takamatsu to Poland and its political context.
subfiles.from: John C. Wiley (Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Warsaw)
subfiles.summary: Chargé Wiley reports Prince and Princess Takamatsu's October 7-12, 1930 visit to Poland, their official receptions, and press comment on shared Japanese-Polish interests regarding the Soviet Union.
subfiles.title: Visit of Prince and Princess Takamatsu to Poland

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding Ambassador Debuchi's conference with Secretary Stimson concerning Prince Takamatsu's U.S. tour.
subfiles.from: Henry L. Stimson (Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: File note on the January 29, 1931 Debuchi-Stimson conversation about arrangements for Prince and Princess Takamatsu's spring 1931 U.S. visit.
subfiles.title: Conference Regarding U.S. Visit of Prince and Princess Takamatsu

subfiles.about: Reporting the birth of a daughter to the Empress of Japan and noting the conveyance of felicitations.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Neville reports by telegraph that a daughter was born to the Empress at 12:02 p.m. on March 7, 1931, and states he will convey felicitations pursuant to standard circular instructions. An accompanying State Department memorandum notes that the telegram should be filed pending an official autograph announcement from the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Birth of a Daughter to the Empress of Japan

subfiles.about: Transmitting a copy of the formal diplomatic note of congratulations addressed to Foreign Minister Shidehara on the birth of a princess.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Chargé Neville transmits a copy of Embassy Note No. 54 delivered to Foreign Minister Baron Shidehara on March 7, 1931. The note conveys President Hoover's congratulations to the Emperor and Empress on the birth of their daughter.
subfiles.title: Felicitations Conveyed on the Birth of an Imperial Princess

subfiles.about: Transmitting the Japanese Foreign Minister's note conveying the thanks of the Emperor and Empress for Presidential congratulations.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Forbes transmits Note No. 32/P from Foreign Minister Shidehara dated March 19, 1931. Shidehara conveys the Imperial command communicating the sincere appreciation of the Emperor and Empress to the President of the United States for his kind message of congratulations.
subfiles.title: Imperial Acknowledgment of Congratulations on Birth of Princess

subfiles.about: Reporting on the birth and naming ceremony of Princess Atsuko and discussing the line of succession.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Extract from Despatch No. 192 on the March 7, 1931 birth of the Emperor's fourth daughter, Atsuko, leaving Prince Chichibu heir apparent; notes reactions and the March 13 naming.
subfiles.title: Birth and Naming of Princess Atsuko and Succession Status

subfiles.about: Reporting the return of Prince and Princess Takamatsu to Japan following their tour of Europe and America.
subfiles.from: W. Cameron Forbes (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: File note and extract from Despatch No. 278 recording the return of Prince and Princess Takamatsu from their foreign tour and recalling its purposes.
subfiles.title: Return of Prince and Princess Takamatsu from Foreign Tour

subfiles.about: Reporting Chinese newspaper article insulting the Japanese Imperial House and Japanese Consul General's demands in Canton.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (American Consul General, Canton)
subfiles.summary: Consul General Ballantine reports Japan's Canton consul made four demands, including apology, editor's punishment and suspension, over an article derogatory to the Imperial House.
subfiles.title: Japanese Demands Over Canton Newspaper Article Derogatory to Imperial House

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding visa or school approval for Prince Fumitaka Konoye to attend Lawrenceville Academy.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: File note on a Tokyo telegram requesting expedited approval of Lawrenceville Academy for Prince Fumitaka Konoye's study in the United States.
subfiles.title: Expediting Lawrenceville Academy Approval for Prince Fumitaka Konoye

subfiles.about: Reporting the peaceful settlement of the Canton newspaper controversy concerning the Japanese Imperial House.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (American Consul General, Canton)
subfiles.summary: Consul General Ballantine reports the Japanese Consul General confirmed amicable settlement of the Canton newspaper dispute.
subfiles.title: Amicable Settlement of Canton Newspaper Incident

subfiles.about: Analyzing the background and political ramifications of the Canton newspaper incident and Japanese diplomatic strategy.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine (American Consul General, Canton)
subfiles.summary: Ballantine reports settlement of the Canton newspaper incident over the Taisho Emperor's death, with a memorandum of conversation with Consul General Suma on Chinese politics and Japan's Manchuria and Shanghai actions.
subfiles.title: Negotiations Over Canton Newspaper Incident Concerning the Imperial House

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding the visit of Japanese Imperial Princes and the Fleet to Taiwan.
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham (American Consul, Taihoku)
subfiles.summary: File note on a Taihoku Consulate despatch about the July 1933 visit of Japanese Royal Princes and the Fleet to Taiwan.
subfiles.title: Visit of Royal Princes and Japanese Fleet to Taiwan

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding rumors of Emperor Hirohito abdicating in favor of Prince Chichibu if no male heir is born.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: File note on Despatch No. 515 reporting rumors that Hirohito might abdicate for Prince Chichibu if the Empress bore no son.
subfiles.title: Rumors of Possible Imperial Abdication Over Lack of Male Heir

subfiles.about: Reporting the birth of an Imperial Prince and heir to the Throne of Japan.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew's urgent telegram: the Empress gave birth to a son on the morning of December 23, 1933.
subfiles.title: Birth of a Son to the Empress of Japan

subfiles.about: Congratulating the Emperor and Empress of Japan on the birth of their son.
subfiles.from: Franklin D. Roosevelt (President of the United States)
subfiles.summary: President Roosevelt's telegram to the Emperor and Empress congratulating them on the birth of an Imperial son, with personal wishes from himself and Mrs. Roosevelt.
subfiles.title: President Roosevelt's Felicitations on the Birth of the Crown Prince
subfiles.to: Emperor and Empress of Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Text of radio broadcast remarks delivered by Acting Secretary Phillips celebrating the birth of the Japanese Crown Prince.
subfiles.from: William Phillips (Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Press release of Acting Secretary Phillips's radio address to Japan on the birth of an Imperial son, reading Roosevelt's congratulatory telegram.
subfiles.title: Address by Acting Secretary Phillips on the Birth of an Imperial Son

subfiles.about: Reporting the clear reception and positive impact in Tokyo of Acting Secretary Phillips's radio broadcast.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Grew wires Phillips that his broadcast was received clearly in Tokyo at 7:05 a.m. and had a very helpful effect.
subfiles.title: Clear Reception of Secretarial Radio Broadcast in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Conveying seasonal greetings and congratulations on the birth of the Imperial son to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires.
subfiles.from: William Phillips (Under Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Phillips's personal letter to Japanese Chargé Taketomi congratulating him on the birth of an Imperial Prince and sending New Year wishes.
subfiles.title: Congratulations to the Japanese Chargé d'Affaires
subfiles.to: Toshihiko Taketomi (Japanese Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Washington)

subfiles.about: Arrangements, internal memoranda, and draft text for the NBC international broadcast honoring the Japanese royal birth.
subfiles.from: National Broadcasting Company / State Department officials
subfiles.summary: A file of correspondence and internal departmental memoranda coordinating William Phillips's participation in an NBC international radio broadcast celebrating the royal birth. Includes NBC executive Vincent Callahan's formal invitation, Division of Far Eastern Affairs memos recommending participation, and final draft speaking remarks incorporating Roosevelt's telegram.
subfiles.title: Coordination of NBC Special Broadcast for the Imperial Birth

subfiles.about: Expressing appreciation on behalf of the Japanese public for Acting Secretary Phillips's broadcast speech.
subfiles.from: Central Broadcasting Bureau, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Tokyo's Central Broadcasting Bureau cables thanks to Phillips; listeners were deeply impressed by his clearly heard address.
subfiles.title: Appreciation from Central Broadcasting Bureau of Tokyo

subfiles.about: Expressing thanks for Acting Secretary Phillips's congratulatory letter on the royal birth.
subfiles.from: Toshihiko Taketomi (Japanese Chargé d'Affaires a.i., Washington)
subfiles.summary: Chargé Taketomi acknowledges Phillips's letter of December 26, expressing warm personal gratitude for the American congratulations on the birth of an Imperial son and reciprocating New Year greetings.
subfiles.title: Japanese Chargé's Appreciation for American Congratulations

subfiles.about: Transmitting Station JOAK's appreciation message and exchanging reciprocal thanks for the broadcast's success.
subfiles.from: Toshihiko Taketomi / William Phillips
subfiles.summary: Chargé Taketomi transmits a message from Mr. Nakayama, President of Tokyo radio station JOAK, expressing gratitude for the flawless international broadcast. On January 3, 1934, Acting Secretary Phillips replies, expressing delight at the evident appreciation and technical success of the broadcast throughout Japan.
subfiles.title: Exchange of Thanks Regarding Success of International Broadcast

subfiles.about: Citizen letter advocating spiritual renewal and goodwill gifts for the Japanese Crown Prince, with departmental reply.
subfiles.from: William L. Norton / Stuart J. Fuller
subfiles.summary: William L. Norton of Toledo writes to Roosevelt proposing a gift to the new Japanese Crown Prince to foster peace; Stuart J. Fuller formally acknowledges.
subfiles.title: Public Suggestion for Goodwill Token to Japanese Crown Prince
subfiles.to: Franklin D. Roosevelt / William L. Norton

subfiles.about: Commentary on Ambassador Grew's political despatch, recalling the 1930 assassination of Prime Minister Hamaguchi.
subfiles.from: Department of State officer (B.H.D.)
subfiles.summary: Internal memorandum on Grew's Despatch No. 639 endorsing his view that the Emperor lacks sympathy for military extremists, and recalling the writer's 1930 condolences after Hamaguchi's shooting.
subfiles.title: Departmental Memorandum on Ambassador Grew's Political Despatch

subfiles.about: In-depth analysis of the stabilizing political effects of the Crown Prince's birth on Japanese military and factional strife.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew assesses the far-reaching internal political significance of the birth of Crown Prince Akihito. He explains how the lack of a direct male heir had fueled chauvinistic military factions, attempts against the Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal, and rumors of forcing the Emperor to abdicate in favor of Prince Chichibu. The birth of a son ends succession plots, bolsters moderate court advisers, and reinforces domestic stability, with public goodwill enhanced by President Roosevelt's prompt congratulatory message.
subfiles.title: Political Significance of the Birth of the Crown Prince

subfiles.about: Reporting the nationwide celebrations and naming ceremonies in Tokyo following the birth of the Crown Prince.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (American Ambassador, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Extract from Despatch No. 635 on public rejoicing after the Crown Prince's birth on December 23, 1933, and Tokyo's December 29 celebrations when he was named Akihito.
subfiles.title: Celebration and Naming of the Crown Prince of Japan

subfiles.about: Transmitting Emperor Hirohito's autograph letter announcing the birth and formal naming of Crown Prince Akihito.
subfiles.from: Hiroshi Saito (Japanese Ambassador, Washington)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Saito transmits Emperor Hirohito's autograph letter to Roosevelt, with translation, announcing the birth of Prince Akihito on December 23, 1933, named December 29.
subfiles.title: Emperor's Autograph Announcement of the Birth and Naming of the Crown Prince
